title: The Always-Responder estimate disagrees with Table 2
published: Under the unverifiable assumption that both pair members would also have responded if the treatment assignment had been switched, I estimate the ATE among this subgroup to be [[−5.5]] points (SE = 2.5 points).
corrected: Under the unverifiable assumption that both pair members would also have responded if the treatment assignment had been switched, I estimate the ATE among this subgroup to be [[−5.6]] points (SE = 2.5 points).
note: Table 2 prints −0.056 for the same estimate, which is −5.6 points. The estimate is −5.563 points, so the table rounds and the sentence truncates, and the article disagrees with itself about the number a reader would quote. The standard error is 2.482 points and is correct as published.

title: The standard error on the redefined outcome
published: Finally, using the redefined outcome, I estimate the ATE to be a [[6]] point decrease in friendliness (SE = [[1.7]] points).
corrected: Finally, using the redefined outcome, I estimate the ATE to be a [[6.1]] point decrease in friendliness (SE = [[1.8]] points).
note: Table 2 prints no standard errors, so this figure appears in the article only here. The standard error is 1.756 points, which rounds to 1.8; the sentence truncates it, as the sentence before it does. The point estimate is a decrease of 6.100 points, which the sentence truncates to a whole number in the same way; it is given here at the decimal the corrected standard error is given to.

title: The naive estimate is printed without its unit
note: Found while preparing the remastered edition. Every other quantity in the sentence and in the one before it is given in points, and Table 2 prints −0.035 for this estimate, which is −3.5 percentage points. The missing word is the one the rest of the paragraph uses, so it is supplied rather than guessed at, and the figure itself is correct as published.

title: Table 2's bounds interval drops a digit the rest of its column carries
published: [[Table 2's bounds row, whose 95% confidence interval opens at −0.73]]
corrected: [[−0.730, the same value at the three decimal places the rest of the column is given to]]
note: Found while preparing the remastered edition. The value is not in dispute and no estimate moves: the limit is −0.730, and the five other limits in the same column are printed to three places (−0.075, 0.005, −0.095, −0.027 and 0.726). Line 187 of the deposited `aec_replication_JEPS.R` builds the cell as `paste0("[", round(ci_lower, 3), ", ", round(ci_upper, 3), "]")`, and `round()` returns a numeric that `paste0` converts with `as.character`, which drops a trailing zero; the other limits keep their three places only because none of them ends in one. This is the one cell of Table 2 the maintained rewrite does not return: R 3.6.0 changed `sample()`, so it is reproduced under the archive's own resampling scheme and the sampler the 2018 run used, which is what `maintained/output/text_bootstrap_sampler.csv` records.
